Environment and GPU setup

Verify your Python environment, choose a backend, and complete one tiny CPU simulation.

Install and fetch tables once

Add Packages To add or change a dependency, open MoLab's built-in package manager on the left and enter the package name and version, for example endf-parserpy==0.17.0. The required interaction data download is about 100 MB. The setup cell calls _ = pyrite.fetch_tables() to install missing tables automatically -- see the tables reference. If an existing session reports MF=26/MT=527 photon yield table is missing, open MoLab's package manager, enter endf-parserpy==0.17.0, and restart the kernel. NVIDIA GPU: start with CPU. If your MoLab session offers an NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000, first add pyrite-mc[nvidia] as a dependency, then select that GPU in the Molab menu before restarting the kernel.

data.text/markdown:
Choose the backend before import

The first code cell sets PYRITE_MC_BACKEND to cpu unless the environment already selected another backend. For GPU execution, set it to cuda before importing PyRITE. Restart the kernel after changing the backend or installing CuPy.

Continue

This tiny, fixed-seed run verifies that the selected backend can produce finite, nonzero spectral data with the installed tables. Continue with 01 — Your first X-ray spectrum. Keep the core sequence on CPU until workload size justifies a GPU. GPU outputs can differ across architectures; compare physically meaningful quantities with justified tolerances, not exact random-history identity.
